extracted.intended_audience: Graduate student applicants to the DOE SCGSR program, collaborating DOE laboratory scientists, and primary graduate thesis advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and program requirements for applying to, being selected for, and participating in the U.S. DOE Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) supplemental award program, including eligibility, application materials, reviewer selection criteria, award terms, and participant responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission deadline and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Your complete application must be submitted online by May 6, 2026, 5:00PM ET. This includes completion of all required application fields, official graduate transcripts, research proposal, and 2 letters of support (one from your graduate thesis advisor and the other from your collaborative DOE laboratory research scientist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both letters must be received before the deadline. The application is not submitted until you press “Submit” on the final submission page. The online system will indicate a 'Submitted' status and show a blue check mark when successfully submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online application only
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted electronically through the online application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications sent to DOE by email or postal mail will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save/edit application functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: You can save your application and work on it anytime during the application period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Status page will show incomplete elements. You can send reminders to letter writers via the system. You must press final 'Submit' to submit the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / Residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be a U.S. citizen or Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) at the time of applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If selected, proof of U.S. citizenship or permanent residency will be required upon award notification. Foreign students on student visas (F1) are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: LPR site-access caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with LPR status are encouraged to contact their DOE National Laboratory/facility of interest during application due to lead time for foreign national access processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers are subject to change based on approval for site access prior to the planned start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ph.D. candidacy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of application submission, applicants must have obtained their Ph.D. candidacy and have a defined graduate thesis project and advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide official proof of candidacy. Acceptable proofs: (1) official signed letter from Registrar; or (2) official signed letter from Department Chair describing candidacy requirements, how the applicant fulfills them, and the date/term candidacy was achieved. If transcripts do not explicitly show candidacy status/date, additional official proof is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time enrollment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be enrolled in a qualified graduate program as a full-time graduate student at an accredited U.S. college or university at the time of application and must remain full-time during the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DOE SCGSR will adopt the definition of full-time enrollment used by the student’s graduate institution (typical graduate norm ~9 credits). Awardees are responsible for any tuition/fees required to remain enrolled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified Graduate Program definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Qualified Graduate Program must: be a Ph.D. degree program that requires a research thesis/dissertation; be in specified fields (physics, chemistry, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer/computational science, and areas of environmental sciences); and the area of graduate research must be clearly within areas supported by DOE Office of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain degree programs are NOT eligible (joint BS/MS, DVM, MBA, MD, joint MD/PhD, JD, or joint JD/PhD). Biomedical sciences, social sciences, and some environmental science areas are not supported—check the Qualified Graduate Program list and DOE priority research areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior/current DOE lab research exclusion (same site)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students currently conducting research at a DOE laboratory/facility are not eligible to apply to conduct research at the same DOE laboratory/facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may apply to conduct part of their thesis research at a different DOE laboratory/facility. Past short collaborations (<3 months) at a lab do not bar eligibility to return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior on-site research duration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who have had past research collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist may apply provided that past graduate research experiences at that laboratory/facility were less than 3 months in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If past on-site collaboration exceeded three months total, the student is not eligible to apply to work with that lab under SCGSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time student exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Part-time graduate students are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must be enrolled full-time at an accredited institution to apply and to remain eligible to receive the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple awards and cumulative duration cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals may receive more than one SCGSR award during their graduate education provided the cumulative total of award periods does not exceed 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a current awardee competes successfully for a new award, they must complete the current award and fulfill all obligations before the new award's start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-developed research proposal required
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must submit a co-developed SCGSR research proposal as a PDF uploaded into the online application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal must be uploaded by the application deadline. When first uploaded or updated, automated notifications are sent to the graduate thesis advisor and collaborating DOE laboratory scientist. Applicants are responsible for communicating updates and obtaining approvals from both.

rubrics_metrics.name: No supplemental materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit supplemental materials such as publications or research results with your application; they will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations of publications and awards (no more than 3 for each) should be listed in the appropriate section of the online application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official graduate transcripts requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must upload a copy of your official graduate transcripts to your online application. Undergraduate transcripts are not requested or required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official transcripts must be stamped with the college/university Registrar seal and uploaded as PDF. Unofficial copies are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript PII redaction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted official transcripts must have all Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth redacted or removed prior to uploading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are considered protected PII. Any application found to contain PII (SSNs or DOBs) will be deemed non-compliant and will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support required and origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Two letters of support are required: one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters must be submitted through the online form provided by the application system. The applicant initiates the request using the Request Letters of Support tool. Both letters must be received by the application deadline. Letters sent in any other format will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support submission constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support must be submitted electronically via the one-time online form; they cannot be saved and returned to later, cannot be submitted by email/post, and cannot be edited after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended letter writers draft in a word processor and then paste into the form. Once submitted, the access code is disabled and the letter cannot be edited or reprinted (except immediate print at end of submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support content prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: The online letter of support form requests: how long they have known the applicant; the applicant’s preparedness for the proposed research; the scientific merit of the proposed project as an integral part of the overall thesis; how the project will take advantage of DOE capabilities; verification that they have read and approved the proposal; and verification that access to any scientific user facilities will be secured prior to the project start (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thesis advisors are also asked to verify they understand program requirements (e.g., full-time enrollment during the award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility for letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for requesting letters of support through the online system and for reminding their thesis advisor and collaborating scientist to submit letters before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After requesting a letter via the system, applicants receive an email confirming it was sent; the program cannot know if the recipient opened the email until the letter is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start/End date and blackout date constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Start and End Dates should be business days (not holidays or weekends) and must fall within the published Earliest and Latest Start Dates for proposed project periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holidays refer to those recognized by the host DOE laboratory/facility (generally federal holidays). Overall project duration (including start and end dates) must be at least 3 consecutive months and not more than 12 consecutive months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing award period dates (modification policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to Start/End dates may be considered only under exceptional circumstances with valid evidence and support from both the Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist and the Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be submitted to the SCGSR Program Manager at least 20 business days in advance of the expected change and include signed letters of consent from both collaborators. The overall project period must remain the same as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time attendance at host laboratory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are expected to conduct research and maintain a full-time schedule at their host DOE laboratory/facility during the award term, while remaining full-time enrolled at their graduate institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees should avoid obligations that interrupt SCGSR research. Any expected interruptions must be reported to the Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist and SCGSR Program Manager. Violations may jeopardize the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility when accepting non-SCGSR host appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not eligible for an SCGSR award if they have accepted a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host DOE laboratory/facility (e.g., hourly paid intern, temporary, or full-time position) after the application close and before award offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this occurs after application but before award offer, the student becomes ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and merit review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications undergo eligibility and compliance review; eligible and compliant applications are reviewed by experts at the DOE host laboratory using established merit review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for award is based on merit review results and other program policy factors (portfolio balance, availability of funds, etc.). See 'Application Evaluation and Selection' for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend and travel award limits and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are eligible for a monthly stipend up to $3,600 and reimbursement for inbound and outbound travel to/from the host DOE lab up to a total of $3,000 (if distance is more than 50 miles one way).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final award is based on assessment of individual situation with factors including duration of proposed research, location of home residence, and concurrent federal funding. Reimbursements are made according to standard DOE travel policy. Stipends are paid monthly by direct deposit; ORISE provides payment setup instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No supplies or conference travel support
rubrics_metrics.description: The SCGSR award does not provide support for supplies/materials needed for the project or for conference travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss supplies/materials support with the Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist and Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor early. Except inbound/outbound travel to host lab, no other travel supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax responsibility for stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend payments may be taxable in full or in part; DOE/ORISE does not withhold taxes from these payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each awardee is personally responsible for tax preparation and payment. This statement is informational and not legal/tax advice; consult a tax advisor or the IRS for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing/lodging responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees are responsible for arranging and paying for their own lodging during the award term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housing options depend on the host lab; some sites have onsite or secured housing while others require independent arrangements. Contact the DOE Laboratory/Facility POC for local options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit an end-of-award report; for awards greater than 6 months, a mid-term progress report is also required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting templates are provided and reports should be submitted through the online system. Progress and final reports should be reviewed by the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of WDTS/SCGSR support
rubrics_metrics.description: All published reports, journal articles, or professional presentations based on research conducted during the award should carry a specific acknowledgment of DOE WDTS/SCGSR support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required acknowledgment text is provided on the page and must be used to maintain federally-mandated assessment and reporting accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborating DOE laboratory scientist employment eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists must be employed by the DOE laboratory/facility with their salary and benefits provided by that laboratory/facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may have joint appointments with academia but must have the DOE lab as employer and spend at least 50% of their time at the DOE lab. Postdoctoral researchers may serve as collaborating scientists only if their committed tenure at the lab exceeds the proposed project length and supervisor contact info is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborating DOE laboratory scientist role/responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborating scientists are expected to assist with lab access procedures, provide guidance/mentorship, oversee full-time attendance, provide workspace/equipment/resources, review reports, serve as resource for training, and coordinate with local POC and program manager to resolve issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborating scientists must oversee fulfillment of the full-time attendance requirement and will receive additional guidance from the SCGSR program prior to the award start date. Collaborating scientists are not paid by SCGSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor responsibilities (application)
rubrics_metrics.description: As the primary graduate thesis advisor you are expected to guide the student in identifying a host lab and collaborating scientist, provide guidance on the research proposal, ensure the proposed scope does not duplicate active grants, approve the final proposal, and submit a letter of support via the online system before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisor letter form asks about how long they have known the applicant, preparedness, importance to thesis, verification of approval of the proposal, and understanding of program requirements (e.g., full-time enrollment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor responsibilities (participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a student receives an SCGSR award, the advisor remains responsible for supporting the student during the award (ensuring tuition/fees for full-time enrollment are provided) and providing ongoing mentorship remotely while the student conducts research at the DOE lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors should coordinate with collaborating DOE lab scientists and the awardee to support successful completion of the project and fulfillment of award obligations.
